fields.label: waste cask
fields.description:
A heavy sealed drum of old, dangerous waste — dose-bearing slag, spent cells, contaminated sludge — the kind of thing the Wasteland has been collecting for centuries.

It is safe while it is whole. Breached below half its integrity it leaks tox gas and pollution until it is moved into a powered sealed cask bay or off the map, and a cask destroyed outright spills everything at once. Left outdoors it weathers.

A sealed cask bay holds casks safely, and a tamed sloghog or sootgrazer beside the bay can digest them into bezoars or soot bricks. A cask can also be dug back into the ground — illegally.

fields.label: the Wastes
fields.description: Where rivers die, everything they carried is concentrated into salt and brine; where the sky's exhaust falls, nothing ever washes it away. Nothing here recycles -- water doesn't leave, fallout doesn't wash, history doesn't decay. The wildlife is wretched and mutated as the rule, extremophile-odd as the exception; the danger is the ground, the air and the water, never the creatures. They merely adapt, struggle, and mostly fail.

fields.label: brine shock
fields.description: A jolt from a brineleech eaten raw — the charge it kept for its own defense, working on you instead. It passes.

fields.letterText:
Something the size of a hill is coming: a middenshell, twenty paces across, wearing a shell of everything it ever ate.

It is not hostile. But it does not stop, it flattens whatever lies in its path, its tentacles drag in objects near it, and standing close to it doses you.

middenshell track
fields.description: Ground crushed flat and glazed by a middenshell's passing: a trench twenty paces wide of packed crust, slag and metal-salt smear. Nothing grows in it.

fields.label: middenshell edge scar
fields.description: Where a middenshell dragged itself off the map: the ground torn open and gouged into ridges, dark with its leakage. A landmark for as long as anyone lives here.

fields.label: hypersaline deep water
fields.description: Deep brine, dead-river salt and old contamination concentrated past any use. Nothing swims here that was not built for it.

fields.label: hypersaline chest-deep water
fields.description: Fast, chest-deep brine feeding one of the dead rivers' last stretches before the salt takes it. Corrosive at length, not on contact.

fields.label: hypersaline shallow water
fields.description: The margin of a brine pool, salt-crusted at the edge, mineral beds visible through the shallows. Something living may share the pool with you.

fields.label: hypersaline shallow moving water
fields.description: A dying river's last shallow reach, running slower with every tile toward the pool it feeds. Salt-crusted at the margin, mineral beds visible underneath.

fields.label: waste tipping pad
fields.description: A marker post that licenses the ground around it as a waste tipping pad. A licensed convoy lands its casks inside the marked area. Select it to see the area.

fields.label: middenshell
fields.description:
A colossal, ancient excretor twenty paces across — the sloghog's deep-time cousin grown into geography. A soft tube body lives inside a long irregular shell of accreted minerals fused into scavenged debris, hull scraps and its own vitrified bezoars: centuries of everything it ate, worn as architecture.

It is never hostile. It does not fight and barely notices you. But it crawls, slowly and without stopping, and whatever lies in its path is flattened or swallowed. Now and then a scaled tentacle lashes out and drags a nearby object — a crate, a door, a wall — into the shell. It will not touch a gravship.

It comes as a procession: hours before it arrives the crust trembles and loose metal creeps toward the edge it will enter by. It crosses the map on one slow line and leaves by the far edge, pressing a permanent track behind it strewn with hot footprints, shell flakes and small bezoars. A stockpile holding waste draws it off its line.

Standing near it is a dose: the ground it concentrates leaks off the shell as toxic buildup.

Killed, its shell hardens where it falls into a quarry of contaminant and vitrified bezoars, and the dose stays with the stone.

fields.label: middenshell carcass
fields.description: Hardened shell of a dead middenshell: fused slag, debris and layered metal-salt contamination, set like stone. Mined for contaminant bezoars. Working it doses the miner.

fields.label: vitrified middenshell seam
fields.description: A glassy black-green seam in a dead middenshell's shell, where its bezoars fused under their own heat. Mined for vitrified bezoars — the richest prize in the Wasteland. Working it doses the miner.

fields.label: sealed cask bay
fields.description:
A powered, shielded rack for waste casks. While its seals have power, anything stored in it stays contained — breached casks included — and it neither weathers nor leaks. Its readout shows seal integrity, internal heat, stored dose and whether it is safe to fly.

Without power the seals run down; below half integrity, or with the bay itself shot up, it starts to leak.

Built on a gravship's substructure it flies with the ship, but the ship will not launch while the bay is unpowered, damaged or running hot, or while any waste cask is loose on the deck.

Switch on processing and a tamed sloghog or sootgrazer standing beside the bay will digest the casks, one by one, into bezoars or soot bricks.

fields.label: sparkcrab bed
fields.description: A crust of salt-white mineral over a shallow shelf, crawling with plate-scrapers just under the surface. Break the crust and they scatter for the taking.

fields.label: brineleech bed
fields.description: A stack of mineral wafers half-buried in the pool floor, salt-white and dark by turns — the owner, dormant and heavy, waiting under the crust. Mining it out is the only way anyone gets one without a dry line and a lot of patience.

fields.label: spent electrode bed
fields.description: A brineleech's discarded plates, gone still and cold, pressed into the mineral crust by seasons of brine. Rarer than a living bed and worth the extra digging.

fields.label: irradiated hull
fields.description: A crashed hull section, still hot. Nobody has come for it because nobody wants to stand next to it, so most of the metal is still there. Deconstruct it for valuable resources.

fields.label: irradiated tank
fields.description: A ruptured tank lying in the ash, its shell stained and warm to the counter. Deconstruct it for valuable resources.

fields.label: warcasket sarcophagus
fields.description: A Junker who went in for the core and did not come out, still sealed inside an adjusted warcasket. The suit kept everything it closed over: the tools, the half-extracted fuel core still in its grips, and the dose. Deconstruct it for valuable resources, if you can stand next to it long enough.

fields.label: hot middenshell footprint
fields.description: A smear pressed into the ground by a middenshell's underside, still warm and faintly smoking with its own decay heat.

fields.label: middenshell shell flakes
fields.description: Plates of accreted mineral, slag and fused junk shed from a middenshell's shell as it grinds along.

fields.label: waste cask
fields.description:
A heavy sealed drum of old, dangerous waste — dose-bearing slag, spent cells, contaminated sludge — the kind of thing the Wasteland has been collecting for centuries.

It is safe while it is whole. Breached below half its integrity it leaks tox gas and pollution until it is moved into a powered sealed cask bay or off the map, and a cask destroyed outright spills everything at once. Left outdoors it weathers.

A sealed cask bay holds casks safely, and a tamed sloghog or sootgrazer beside the bay can digest them into bezoars or soot bricks. A cask can also be dug back into the ground — illegally.

fields.label: sparkcrab
fields.description: A salt-white, flat-bodied scraper the size of a thumb, living on the mineral beds under the brine and grazing the crust the brineleech lay down. It carries a charge — a small one; picking one up bare-handed is a tingle and a lesson. They swarm on a carcass in the pool and strip it, and on a brineleech that has spent its charge, which is how the pool's owner eventually dies. Edible after a long soak.

fields.label: brineleech
fields.description: The owner. A forearm-long, plated, sea-cucumber-shaped thing whose body is a stack of living electrode wafers, salt-white and mineral-dark by turns, lying on the bed of a hypersaline pool and running on the ion gradient between the brine and the metal beneath it. It discharges as defense. The pool you want to mine has one, and it is a capacitor, and it does not want you there. Landed — carefully, on a dry line, by people who have done it before — it goes on discharging for an hour. Cooked, it is meat. Raw, it is a lesson.

fields.label: brine plate
fields.description: A stacked mineral wafer, salt-white and dark by turns, pried off a brineleech that has already spent its charge — or found loose on a pool floor, which is the same thing a season later. It still holds a whisper of charge; touch two together in the dark and they spark. Traders who buy oddities want it.

fields.label: contaminant bezoar
fields.description: A dense fist-sized lump of refined metal-salt contamination, coughed up whole by an excretor animal that spent days walking it out of poisoned ground. Heavy, layered, faintly waxy — worth real money to the right buyer, and worth keeping in small piles only. A kept herd producing these one stone at a time is the closest thing this ground has to a refinery.

fields.label: vitrified bezoar
fields.description: A rarer, larger grade of contaminant bezoar, mined out of a hardened Middenshell corpse's own accreted shell — glassy black-green vitrified mineral fused with metal-salt layers, deep sickly-radiance seams glowing faintly inside the glass. The richest excretor-refining prize in the biome, priced in the dose you take digging it out.

fields.label: soot brick
fields.description: A compressed brick of fuel-grade soot and ash, pressed out of a sootgrazer that spent the season eating deposition off the flats. Cheap, stackable, burns dirty but burns — and the supply is endless where the sky keeps falling.

fields.label: dosimeter lawn
fields.description: A low mat of sickly, unnervingly vivid moss-lichen. It grows thickest over the hottest ground -- locals read its color and density as a rough gauge of what's buried beneath, and camp where it refuses to grow at all.

fields.label: vault-root tree
fields.description: A squat, gnarled tree whose swollen trunk is seamed with dull metallic veins -- it has spent decades sequestering what it drinks out of the ground into itself. Prospectors call felling one "opening the vault," and know exactly what that name is warning them about.

fields.label: scorched stars
fields.description: Rounder cacti covered in sharp spines. They are often said to look like a burnt star.

fields.label: scumgrass
fields.description: A wiry tussock of grease-slicked grass that grows where cleaner plants die — dull grey-green blades with an oily sheen, tips crusted white with salt. The biome's default green: sparse but firmly rooted, and grazing animals eat it without complaint.

fields.label: tall scumgrass
fields.description: The same wiry, grease-slicked grass where the ground is richest — which here means worst. Waist-high, sight-blocking, salt crust heavier at the tips.

fields.label: pusberry
fields.description: A small tree whose pale berries sit in weeping, wax-sealed sockets — it walls its fruit off from its own sap the way the boilhide walls off poison. Edible once processed; raw is a lesson.

fields.label: boilbulb
fields.description: A ground bulb swollen into a blistered dome, mineral-crusted at the base, faintly warm to the hand. A forage staple for the wretched-many cast and a processed-food input for colonists.

fields.label: wartshrub
fields.description: A knee-high shrub whose bark is one continuous wart-field — sequestration in miniature, locking what it drinks into its galls. Galls harvestable as a low-grade chemical/fuel input.

fields.label: cinderfelt
fields.description: A felt-grey mat that grows only on fresh ash fall. After every storm the flats grow a grey pelt, and where the felt is thickest, the fall was heaviest — which is where the survey, and the dose, is. Fast-growing, short-lived; it dies as the fall compacts.

fields.label: boilhide
fields.description: A herd grazer whose entire hide is a landscape of sealed boils — each one a pocket where its body walled poison off and moved on, antlers fused into a single mineral-crusted club. It grazes the toxic flora of the flats without complaint and runs fast enough that nothing here catches it.

fields.label: gravelgut
fields.description: A low armored slab that eats the ground itself — gravel, glass-crumb, mineral crust — and passes it as smooth sorted pebbles the locals kick apart to read what is buried underneath. Mouthparts worn to polished stone, hide set with a mosaic of swallowed-and-rejected glass. It ignores everything and hits like a wall if pressed.

fields.label: grimewing
fields.description: A wretched, half-bald scavenger bird that rides the storm-thermals — patchy moth-eaten feathers over bare warty grey skin, a salt-stained hooked beak, wing gaps where feathers never grew back. Fresh exhumation after a storm draws it circling: the visible marker that the map got re-dealt, the way the cinderfelt marks the fall. It eats what the storm digs up, never what walks.

fields.label: gripper
fields.description: A fist-sized beetle that files across the flats in caravan lines, hauling scraps of everything back to middens it defends from nobody — carapace pitted like struck flint, salt rime at every seam, forelegs always gripping some scrap or other. It never comes back empty-handed.

fields.label: gristleswarm
fields.description: A knee-high scuttler of gristle and plate that lives in rot-slow country by eating what cannot rot — sinew, hide, bone-rind — and thriving on it. Exposed gristle at the joints gone leathery and grey, back plates crazed like dried mud. A pack fights back as one when one of its own is hurt.

fields.label: soot gristleswarm
fields.description: The gristleswarm of the ash country — the same animal run through the chimney: soot-black, grease-sheened, ember-eyed. Same body, same pack-defense habit, better suited to the cold dark scour's margin.

fields.label: scabspinner
fields.description: A patchy-furred ambusher whose webs are half silk, half scab — it spins over its own sores and over its burrow mouth alike, and both hold. Crusted spinnerets, mange-map bald patches, joints re-silked daily. It hunts the small cast of the flats and flees anything larger.

fields.label: scumslider
fields.description: An oozing slug-bodied thing that lurches forward on two stout tails, three eyes on independent stalks watching every direction at once. It is fat on what nothing else will touch — wart-clustered, salt-stained, mineral-streaked down the flanks — and doing fine on ground that kills cleaner things.

fields.label: slagmole
fields.description: A barrel of muscle built to dig through vitrified crust like frost, its claws worn glassy and its ribbed back set with embedded grit it never sheds. Its shovel-flat face reads the ground it digs; one eye going milky is common and never slows it down.

fields.label: sloghog
fields.description: A warty, barrel-bodied hog that grazes poisoned ground with total contentment and periodically coughs up the poison as a stone worth selling. Wart fields down both flanks, tusks capped in mineral crust, content half-shut eyes. A kept herd is a slow refinery — the closest thing this ground has to livestock.

fields.label: smolderback
fields.description: So hot with its own decay it must dump heat to live — a living furnace that haunts the cold dark scour and cannot stand its own company. Back plates split by glowing seams, snow never lies on it, the ground steams where it beds. Tame one and winter is solved and dosed at once: it heats a shelter all winter, and irradiates it the entire time.

fields.label: sootgrazer
fields.description: A slab-shouldered grazer that works the ash-fall like pasture — it eats deposition itself and presses what it can't burn into brick. Hide the exact grey of settled ash with darker grease-streak shadows it never had rain to earn, nostrils fringed with filter-bristle combs.

fields.label: ash storm
fields.description: Centuries of settled fallout picked up and re-dealt: blinding, abrasive and radiologically live. Anyone caught outside takes a dose; the fall poisons the ground it lands on, and when it passes the drifts have moved — something is buried, something else uncovered. Re-survey after every storm.

fields.label: deadlight halo
fields.description: It arrives quietly. Shadows deepen and double, dosimeters click faster and faster, and a sickly light rims every living thing under the open sky. Then the auroral glow settles over the ground, lit from inside by the fallout it stirs. Less violent than an ash storm, but the ambient dose is raised for as long as it lasts — anyone under open sky soaks it up.

fields.label: cinderwire storm
fields.description: Charged fallout whipped past threshold until the wind itself is radioactive and electric. It announces itself: static crawls over the ground, loose scraps lift and hang in the air, and a deep electrical whine builds. Then it breaks — EMP pulses, plasma lightning, a heavy burying fall, and a severe dose for anyone outside. Found only in the terminator pockets.

alerts.label: Low food
alerts.explanation:
You are dangerously low on food.

    Full bars worth of food in storage: 0
    Colonists and prisoners getting food: 4
    Days worth of food in storage: 0

Grow, buy, find, or kill some food.

alerts.label: Low medicine
alerts.explanation:
You have no medicine left in storage.

Buy more medicine from traders.

alerts.label: Need colonist beds
alerts.explanation:
You have more colonists than you have colonist beds. Someone will lack a place to sleep.

Either make more beds, or change a prisoner bed to a colonist bed.

If you have no resources, sleeping spots are free and can be placed instantly.

alerts.label: Need meal source
alerts.explanation:
You have no way of preparing proper meals from raw food.

Build a stove, campfire, or nutrient dispenser.

(It cannot be in a prison cell, otherwise colonists cannot use it.)

alerts.label: Heatstroke
alerts.explanation:
The following people are suffering from heatstroke:
  - <color=#D09B61FF>Lachi</color>
  - <color=#D09B61FF>Chaz</color>
  - <color=#D09B61FF>Tiffy</color>

Get them to a cooler area. You can cool down rooms with passive coolers or electrical coolers. Deep underground spaces are also naturally cool, if separated from the outdoors by a door.

alerts.label: Colonist left unburied
alerts.explanation:
A colonist is left unburied.

This may negatively affect your colonists' mood.

alerts.label: Need recreation variety
alerts.explanation:
There are only 2 different recreation types available in Colony, but at the current expectations level (low), colonists need 3 different kinds of recreation to remain satisfied. Provide recreation variety supplying a new, different kind of recreation.

<color=#E6E64CFF>Available recreation types</color>:
  - Solitary relaxation
  - Social interaction

<color=#E6E64CFF>Missing recreation types</color>:
  - Dexterity play
  - Cerebral play
  - Television watching
  - Telescope study
  - Music
  - Chemical consumption
  - Food consumption
  - Reading

Note: You can check the recreation type of any item in its stats page, accessible with the 'i' button.

alerts.label: Brawler has ranged weapon
alerts.explanation: One of your colonists has the Brawler personality trait, but is carrying a ranged weapon. This will make them very unhappy.

alerts.label: Open Priest role unfilled
alerts.explanation:
These roles are not filled:
  - <color=#6E61D7FF>Open Priest</color>

You can assign someone a role on their Social tab. You can also select a ritual spot or an altar and click 'Begin role change'. 

If these roles remain empty, the following people will be unhappy:
  - <color=#D09B61FF>Malachai 'Lachi' Rabenhertz</color>
  - <color=#D09B61FF>Chaz Targrin</color>
  - <color=#D09B61FF>Naoko 'Tiffy' Estes</color>
  - <color=#D09B61FF>Samantha 'Sam' Haxton</color>

alerts.label: Major break risk
alerts.explanation:
These colonists are in a very poor mood and may have a major mental break at any time:
  - <color=#D09B61FF>Lachi</color>

These colonists are in a poor mood and may have a minor mental break at any time:
  - <color=#D09B61FF>Chaz</color>
  - <color=#D09B61FF>Tiffy</color>

Check these colonists' Needs tab to see what's bothering them.

To make colonists feel better, you can do things like make them fancy meals, give them more recreation hours per day and nicer recreation objects, place them in beautiful environments, have them drink and smoke, and much more.

alerts.label: Medical treatment needed
alerts.explanation:
These people need medical treatment. Without it, they may die of their wounds, or their wounds may become permanent.
  - <color=#D09B61FF>Lachi</color>

Treat them by sending them to a medical bed.

(First, assign a medical bed by selecting it and toggling it into a medical bed. Then, select the wounded person and right-click on the medical bed to make them a patient.)

alerts.label: 4 colonists idle
alerts.explanation:
These colonists are wandering idly:
  - <color=#D09B61FF>Lachi</color>
  - <color=#D09B61FF>Chaz</color>
  - <color=#D09B61FF>Tiffy</color>
  - <color=#D09B61FF>Sam</color>

You should probably find them something productive to do.

alerts.label: Waste leaking
alerts.explanation:
Breached waste is leaking tox gas and pollution. A breached cask stops leaking inside a powered, intact sealed cask bay; a leaking bay needs power and repair.

Click to see the leak.
